verdict.rationale: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol gives merchants cryptographic HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421, aligned with web-bot-auth) tagged agent-browser-auth/agent-payer-auth, with timestamps/nonces to prevent replay, verified against Visa's published JWKS, explicitly marketed to let merchants 'instantly distinguish a legitimate, credentialed agent from an anonymous bot.' This is backed by a public reference implementation (agent-registry, cdn-proxy, merchant-backend) confirmed live via probe. Missing for 10: independent/third-party merchant case studies showing real-world adoption and differentiation of trust tiers beyond binary signed/unsigned, and confirmation the protocol is out of pilot/GA rather than still emerging.
